https://www.barrons.com/articles/spotify-direct-listing-claims-its-double-the-size-of-apple-music-1519847990 Spotify Direct Listing Claims It’s Double the Size of Apple Music By Feb. 28, 2018 2:59 p.m. ET Text Size Medium Large 
Spotify Technology S.A. , the streaming music service that has 159 million users, this afternoon filed a prospectus to go public in a direct listing on the New York Stock Exchange, and to be listed under the ticker “SPOT.” 
The company will get no proceeds from the direct listing, while there is a "placeholder" amount to be received by selling shareholders, totaling $1 billion. 
The company calls itself the world’s largest steaming music service, and claims it is "nearly double the scale" of Apple ’s ( AAPL ) Apple Music service, its "closest competitor," both by that 159 million total monthly average users, and with 71 million paying “streaming subscribers.” 
The company makes money both from fees from premium subs and from advertising. 
Spotify has eschewed the traditional IPO process, though it has retained Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Allen & Co., for financial advice, separate from the role of the direct market maker. 
Based in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, as far as its official principle address, Spotify had $4 billion in revenue in 2017, an increase of 39%, though its net loss more than doubled to $1.23 billion. Spotify recorded a 26% gross profit margin last year. It generated $109 million of free cash flow last year. 
The company racked up an accumulated deficit of $2.43 billion. 
The prospectus includes a letter from the 35-year-old co-founder and CEO, Daniel Ek, who describes being consumed with music and technology since age 4, and describing ambitions beyond music: 
Music has just been the beginning. We’re an audio first platform—as a top provider of podcasts, we’re also connecting audiences to the conversations that we think will shape the future. And we have even bigger aspirations. We envision a cultural platform where professional creators can break free of their medium’s constraints and where everyone can enjoy an immersive artistic experience that enables us to empathize with each other and to feel part of a greater whole. But to realize this vision, professional creators must be able to earn a fair living doing what they love, where monetization is at the core of a creative proposition and not an afterthought. We care deeply about our creators and our users and we believe Spotify is a win-win for both. 
Correction : A prior version of this post erroneously listed the amount of $1 billion as the amount to be raised by Spotify. In fact, the company receives no proceeds from the direct listing. The provisional amount is indicative of potiential proceeds to certain selling shareholders as a result of the direct listing. My apologies for any confusion caused by the error. Most Popular
